title: Rights and voting
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 3). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

listen.explanationKey: What are three rights of everyone living in the United States?
facts: Some rights belong to everyone living in the United States, not only to citizens. Most of these rights come from the First Amendment.
Freedom of expression: you can share your ideas in many ways, like writing, art or speaking.
Freedom of speech: you can say what you think, even if you disagree with the government.
Freedom of assembly: you can meet together with other people in a peaceful group.
Freedom to petition the government: you can ask the government to change a law or fix a problem.
Freedom of religion: you can practice any religion, or no religion at all.
The right to bear arms: the Second Amendment protects the right to have guns, following the law.
For the test, you need to name three.

readIt.sentence: What do people have the right to do?

listen.explanationKey: Who can vote in federal elections, run for federal office, and serve on a jury in the United States?
facts: Only U.S. citizens can vote in federal elections, run for federal office and serve on a jury.
Four amendments to the Constitution are about who can vote.
They say that a male citizen of any race can vote, that women can vote, that no one has to pay a tax to vote, and that citizens 18 and older can vote.
